data_fields.name: spawn_chance
data_fields.donor_constant: 1-100 byte; roll 1..100, hit if roll <= chance

data_fields.name: spawn_count_max
data_fields.donor_constant: 6-bit field (d1 & 0xff) >> 2 (max 63); count = 1 + rand % max when max > 1

data_fields.name: auto_reset_flag
data_fields.donor_constant: bit 15 of itype; re-arm on re-entry from outside

best_idea: A spawn point rolls once per trigger entry and latches even on a failed roll; the latch is re-armed by a distance-window rule, not a timer.
decision_why: Zones are data and row 23 needs caps, respawn and a despawn grace that this donor lacks; take the one-roll latch, entry trigger, count range and ring placement; reject the superchunk byte serialisation because we load zone data rather than save world state.
acceptance: A server test asserts that a spawn point with chance 50 and count 1..3 rolls once per entry, a failed roll still uses the entry, the point does not roll again until the player leaves its re-arm distance, and each monster lands on a free tile within 5 tiles or the shortfall is counted.
